newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sept foreign currency deposits hit record.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sept foreign currency deposits hit record.

text.p: Taiwan's outstanding foreign currency deposits hit a record T$294.9 billion at the end of September, boosted by the island's continued trade surplus, the central bank said on Monday.
The end-September figure was up from T$290.2 billion at the end of August, the central bank said in a statement.

Exporters, keen to avoid risks in foreign currency exchange, had been growing accustomed to paying for raw material imports directly with foreign currency rather than using Taiwan dollars, central bank officials said.
The bank also linked the rise to inflows of some US$130 million by local firms' issuance overseas of global depositary receipts.
Recently low Taiwan dollar deposit and lending rates also have encouraged investors to hold funds as foreign currency, central bank officials have said.

Foreign currency holdings, which stood at T$123.97 billion in June 1995, surged to T$130.12 billion in July 1995 and T$168.41 billion in August 1995 as rival China carried out a nine-month spate of missile tests and war games near Taiwan to warn the island not to advocate independence.

Military manoeuvres by China, which regards the island as a renegade province, peaked in the runup to Taiwan's historic March 23 presidential election, triggering massive flight to the U.S. dollar and other foreign currencies.
Despite the exchange of holdings to the safe haven of foreign currency, much of the money remained in Taiwan.
Central bank officials have said the actual capital outflow during the Taiwan-China crisis was not as serious as initially feared. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
